title: How upstream firms have quietly revolutionised exploration efficiency | Wood Mackenzie
gist: A report teaser arguing that headline upstream exploration decline is misleading: conventional oil and gas well counts are down 60% from the 2014 peak and total E&A spend is under a third of its all-time high, yet volumes discovered per well have doubled since the early 2000s while per-well spend has fallen and stabilised. Wood Mackenzie's Adam Wilson frames this as a structural efficiency revolution since 2015 that is unlikely to reverse, with returns per exploration dollar now stronger than during the boom years.

insights.claim: Conventional oil and gas exploration well counts are down 60% from their 2014 peak, discovered volumes sit below historical averages and total exploration and appraisal spend is less than a third of its all-time high.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: The activity metrics that drive oilfield services and seismic revenue have collapsed even as exploration outcomes improve — a permanent volume headwind for the service chain.
insights.quote: Oil and gas well counts are down 60% from their 2014 peak, discovered volumes below historical averages and total E&A spend less than a third of its all-time high.
insights.locator: The efficiency revolution: more bang for your exploration buck

insights.claim: Traditional upstream exploration metrics such as spend and well count understate performance because they measure activity rather than productivity, so the sector reads as being in retreat when it is not.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Screening explorers on capex or rig activity systematically misprices the ones that shifted to a quality-over-quantity model.
insights.quote: But these headline figures miss the point.
insights.locator: Is oil and gas exploration in decline?

insights.claim: Volumes discovered per exploration well have doubled since the early 2000s while per-well spend has fallen and stabilised, so the industry now generates a stronger return on each exploration dollar than it did during the boom years.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Exploration is no longer automatically value-destructive — reserve-replacement per dollar is a better screen for E&P equity than drilling activity.
insights.quote: Volumes discovered per well have doubled since the early 2000s, while per-well spend has fallen and stabilised.
insights.locator: The underlying story in conventional exploration

insights.claim: Since 2015 conventional oil and gas exploration has undergone a genuine efficiency revolution rather than a decline, according to analysis of Wood Mackenzie's Lens Subsurface data.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Dates the regime break to 2015 — pre-2015 exploration cost curves are not a valid baseline for modelling future discovery economics.
insights.quote: since 2015, oil and gas exploration has undergone a genuine efficiency revolution
insights.locator: Drawing on data from Wood Mackenzie’s Lens Subsurface

insights.claim: Discovery cost measured as volumes discovered per exploration dollar spent is the metric that reveals the underlying upstream productivity story that spend and well-count data conceal.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete replacement KPI for evaluating explorers: resource per dollar, not dollars deployed.

insights.claim: Explorers that adapted best prioritised quality over quantity and maintained efficient exploration programmes through market cycles rather than chasing the oil price.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Counter-cyclical, steady exploration budgets are the behavioural marker of the outperformers — pro-cyclical capex is the red flag.
insights.quote: Explorers that have navigated this change most effectively have prioritised quality over quantity, and maintained efficient exploration programmes through market cycles rather than chasing the oil price.
insights.locator: Success increasingly depends on identifying high-quality opportunities

insights.claim: Exploration success now depends on identifying high-quality opportunities, screening prospects more effectively and concentrating investment on the most advantaged resources.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Data and subsurface screening capability is now a competitive moat in exploration, favouring operators with the best portfolio-ranking tools.
insights.locator: Success increasingly depends on identifying high-quality opportunities

insights.claim: These structural shifts in oil and gas exploration are unlikely to reverse, meaning the low-activity, high-efficiency model is the durable state rather than a cyclical trough.
insights.speaker: Adam Wilson
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite a return to 2014-style exploration activity levels — service-sector recovery theses built on well-count mean reversion are structurally wrong.
insights.quote: These structural shifts in oil and gas exploration are unlikely to reverse; understanding them is essential for anyone tracking exploration strategy or allocating capital across the upstream sector.
insights.locator: These structural shifts in oil and gas exploration
